audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Tahm Kench levels 2 and 3 while both whys call them Nautilus' first real trade wins.
audit.why: Packet levelChart: Skill, Nautilus, Nautilus, Skill, Skill, Tahm Kench, Tahm Kench. He has no dash and Abyssal Dive is 17-21s, so the early hook window is Nautilus'.
audit.corrected: Both layers set to Skill, Nautilus, Nautilus, Skill, Skill, Tahm Kench, Tahm Kench.

audit.why: Spikes: levels 2-3 kill window, level 6 Depth Charge against Devour, first item Thick Skin turtling, late drain-tank. Matches the chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Slots are swapped throughout: Devour is called his W (it is R) and Abyssal Dive his R (it is W). Grey health is credited to his passive when it is Thick Skin (E, 3s). A 'percent-HP W' is invented — Abyssal Dive is a dive and knock-up with no percent damage, and the passive scales off HIS total health.
audit.why: Riot text: An Acquired Taste builds stacks and at three he can use Devour (R) on an enemy champion; Tongue Lash (Q, 900, 5-7s) heals him and stuns only at three stacks; Abyssal Dive (W, 1000-1200, 17-21s) knocks up; Thick Skin (E, 3s) stores damage taken and converts it to a shield.
audit.corrected: Track your own An Acquired Taste stacks — trade before the third lands or Tongue Lash stuns and Devour becomes available. Abyssal Dive is the 17-21s engage to bait; Thick Skin means burst-and-step-out, plus Grievous Wounds for the out-of-combat healing.

edits.before: Tahm Kench has no dash to dodge your Q, so Levels 2-3 are your window: pull him in, eat the passive root proc with an auto, and layer W splash burn plus E slow before he can waddle off. The catch is his grey-health passive heals back most of what you chip, so a single trade rarely commits him. Bait his Q tongue stun before you throw your own Q, since trading stun-for-stun favors you while his is on cooldown. Do not over-extend chasing a kill he can just regenerate.
edits.after: Tahm Kench has no dash to dodge your Q, so Levels 2-3 are your window: pull him in, eat the passive root proc with an auto, and layer W splash burn plus E slow before he can waddle off. The catch is Thick Skin turns stored damage into a shield every 3 seconds, so one trade rarely commits him. Watch your An Acquired Taste stacks — Tongue Lash only stuns at three, so trade before the third lands. Do not chase a kill he can just regenerate.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 stay roughly even. Your W shield and E let you keep zoning him off CS, and at 6 Depth Charge gives you an undodgeable knock-up to start a gank, his sideways waddle cannot escape a homing ult. But respect his W Devour: if he eats you while your combo is committed and a jungler is near, he flips the all-in. Use your CC chain to set up your jungler rather than solo-killing, because his grey health and percent-HP W make a clean solo kill hard once he has any HP item.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 stay roughly even. Your W shield and E let you keep zoning him off CS, and at 6 Depth Charge gives you an undodgeable knock-up to start a gank, his sideways waddle cannot escape a homing ult. But respect Devour (R): at three An Acquired Taste stacks he eats you mid-combo and flips the all-in with a jungler near. Use your CC chain to set up your jungler rather than solo-killing, because Thick Skin makes a clean solo kill hard once he has an HP item.

edits.before: This is where he reclaims the lane. Once Tahm has an item or two his grey-health passive and percent-HP W simply out-last your CC chain — you lock him down, he survives it, then sustains back up. Your tank damage flatlines while his drain-tank profile only gets stickier. He also out-roams you hard with R Abyssal Dive, making cross-map plays your immobile engage kit can never answer. Trade your CC for objectives and peel for your carries; do not expect to win the straight 1v1 anymore.
edits.after: This is where he reclaims the lane. Once Tahm has an item or two Thick Skin's stored grey health simply out-lasts your CC chain — you lock him down, he shields through it, then sustains back up. Your tank damage flatlines while his drain-tank profile only gets stickier. Devour also lets him pull an ally straight out of your engage, an answer your immobile kit can never match. Trade your CC for objectives and peel for your carries; do not expect to win the straight 1v1.

edits.after: Each of his hits stacks An Acquired Taste on you, and at three stacks his Tongue Lash stuns you for free.

edits.before: Track Tahm Kench's Abyssal Dive: His escape + shield. Trade when down. When it is down — Q-E + R him.
edits.after: Abyssal Dive is his 17-21s dive; Tongue Lash stuns only at three stacks — Q-E + R him in that window.

edits.before: - Tahm Kench Abyssal Dive: matchup-defining — His escape + shield. Trade when down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Tahm Kench Abyssal Dive: 17-21s dive and knock-up from 1000-1200 range. Trade while it is spent. - Tongue Lash: 5-7s, stuns at three stacks. - Depth Charge: the win condition, kill windows only.

notes: Slot map corrected everywhere: Devour is R (needs three An Acquired Taste stacks on the target), Abyssal Dive is W, Thick Skin is E and owns the grey health. The invented 'percent-HP W' is gone — the passive scales off his own total health, not yours.
